coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 4
record.summary: Planned residential block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan with a stepped height envelope of 65 ft and 85 ft; no design review approval or construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built (no design-review approval or construction start found; the 2024 annual compliance report records environmental remediation of the Project's 'Tank Farm Area and Block 4', contracted in Q3 2021) and no Assessor lot of its own was found: DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows its footprint within a much larger active lot, 4175028 (1241 Delaware St, about 21,900 sq m, recorded 2022-08-30), which also overlaps the Block 3 and Block 9 footprints. Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see the mapping log in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record)), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 by georeferencing against many real-street control points. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third revision) by detecting the block colours consistently across the whole block layout at once. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth revision) after fixing a mis-measured control point -- see the mapping log.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, final (February 26, 2020), Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. DataSF Parcels (checked 2026-09-29) shows this footprint within the much larger active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St), not a lot of its own.
notes.regulatory_context: The D4D's Permitted Uses table (Table 3.1.1) confirms residential is permitted here (Laboratory and Life Science are not). Figure 6.2.3 of the final D4D gives Block 4 two height limits by its colour-coded labels, 85 ft and 65 ft; the '100'MAX' label sits on a dimension line (a plan extent of the 85 ft zone), not a height, and Standard 6.2.2 places Block 4 among the lowrise buildings (up to 100 feet). The D4D's text on Figure 1.6.4 names Block 4, on the waterfront, among its 'differentiated buildings'. No construction-start source found.

facts.value: Residential permitted; Institutional (hospital not permitted; basement to mezzanine only in majority-residential buildings), Retail (hotel not permitted; basement to 2nd floor only) and Non-Retail Sales/Services (basement, ground floor and mezzanine only) uses permitted with those floor limits; Laboratory and Life Science Not Permitted (D4D final Table 3.1.1 and its notes 1, 2, 7 and 8)

stepped envelope of 65 ft and 85 ft across different portions of the block, per the colour-coded labels in the D4D's Figure 6.2.3 (the '100'MAX' label is a plan dimension line, not a height); Standard 6.2.2 places Block 4 among the 'Lowrise buildings' (up to 100 feet)

Not listed among the six Phase 1 blocks (2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15) named in the 2024 annual compliance report; the same report (p.32) says the Project contracted Pacific States Environmental Contractors in Q3 2021 as general contractor for environmental remediation of the Project's 'Tank Farm Area and Block 4', which appears to refer to this masterplan block but is not defined in the report, so it is not used as a source for other facts here
Named in the D4D's Figure 1.6.4 text among the 'differentiated buildings' that stand out from the general urban fabric (Block 4, on the waterfront)

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement that first names Block 4 as a development block under the adopted Design for Development's Land Use Table; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date

changes.text: Block 4's record and map notes no longer say the D4D shows a 100 ft envelope: on Figure 6.2.3 the '100' MAX' label is a dimension line, and the block's colour-coded height limits are 85 ft and 65 ft. Its expected completion is now 2029, from SocketSite's October 2020 schedule table (Phase 2, vertical development 2028-2029), instead of the 2035 whole-project target. The permitted-uses fact now states the floor limits in Table 3.1.1, the D4D's own use of 'differentiated buildings' for Block 4 is recorded, and the 2024 annual report's 'Tank Farm Area and Block 4' remediation is described as the Project's own contract, not an unrelated PG&E job. The parcel note now says the footprint lies within active lot 4175028 (1241 Delaware St), sources cite the final D4D instead of a dead 2019 draft link, and the D4D publisher is shown as SF Planning.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 4; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

The 2024 annual compliance report (p.32) refers to remediation of the Project's 'Tank Farm Area and Block 4' by its contractor Pacific States; it appears to mean this masterplan block, but the report does not define 'Block 4', so it is not used as a source for this record's other facts.
Block 4's 2028-2029 window comes from a 2020 press table (SocketSite); no current Block 4 schedule was found.
